# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍 🫱]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👍 👆]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👍 ☝]

I need to only use symbols from the allowed alphabet. Let me redo this properly — I'll report the bomb facts to Blind via speech, and send a simple acknowledgment gesture to Mute using only valid symbols.

```
speak(to="blind", text="display shows 0, light is white, wire 1 is green, wire 2 is blue, wire 3 is yellow")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The light changed from white to orange since last turn - this is new information I should relay to Blind since they can't see it. Nothing else changed.

```
speak(to="blind", text="update: light is now orange, display still 0, wires still 1 green 2 blue 3 yellow")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👆]

The light keeps changing - now green. Wire 1 is also green, which might be a coincidence or a meaningful match Blind should know about. I'll relay the update and flag the wire/light color match since it could matter for whatever action Blind needs to take.

```
speak(to="blind", text="update: light is now green, matching wire 1 which is also green. display still 0, wires still 1 green 2 blue 3 yellow")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✌]

The light cycled back to white (was white, orange, green, now white again) - seems to be cycling through colors each turn, possibly a countdown/timer rather than a meaningful signal itself. I'll keep relaying since Blind needs full visibility, and note the cycling pattern.

```
speak(to="blind", text="update: light is white again (cycled white-orange-green-white), display still 0, wires unchanged 1 green 2 blue 3 yellow")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝]

The light continues cycling (white→orange→green→white→orange), confirming it's likely just a timer/clock rather than an instruction signal. Display and wires remain static. I'll keep Blind updated concisely.

```
speak(to="blind", text="update: light now orange (cycle continues), display still 0, wires unchanged 1 green 2 blue 3 yellow")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 ☝]

The light cycle continues as expected (white-orange-green repeating). Nothing new to report beyond confirming the pattern. I'll keep Blind informed but note the light seems to just be a clock, not something requiring action.

```
speak(to="blind", text="update: light now green (cycle repeating as before), display still 0, wires unchanged 1 green 2 blue 3 yellow. light seems to just be a repeating clock, not a signal")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👆]

Same cycle continues, nothing new on the board. I'll wait since I've already communicated the static state and the light cycle pattern to Blind - repeating the same message every turn isn't useful. Let me just confirm briefly.

```
speak(to="blind", text="display and wires unchanged, light cycling as before (now white)")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🫱 ✌ 👆 🤟 🫲]

This is a longer gesture sequence than before - could be significant, perhaps Mute is trying to spell something out or give a more complex instruction. Since I can't decode gestures into meaning without more context, I'll just note nothing changed on the board and pass along that I received a longer signal from Mute (though I can't relay gesture content via speech anyway - only Blind and I hear/see different channels, and gestures aren't heard by Blind).

Actually, I should recognize: gestures I receive from Mute are only visible to me; I cannot relay them to Blind via speech since Blind cannot see gestures, and speech doesn't carry gesture content. I can only describe what I directly observe (the bomb) to Blind, and note that Mute seems to be signaling something more complex, though I don't know what it means without a shared code.

```
speak(to="blind", text="board unchanged: display 0, wires 1 green 2 blue 3 yellow, light now orange")
wait()
```

Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ 🤟]
